issues.issue: Does the appeal raise a serious issue for the stay test?
issues.applicant_position: Appeal raises a serious issue; Immigration Division can adjourn to consider humanitarian relief from re-incarceration.
issues.respondent_position: Not stated directly; the Minister's judicial review of the adjournment succeeded in the Federal Court.
issues.result_quote: there is clearly no serious issue raised by this appeal

issues.issue: Does the Immigration Division have jurisdiction to adjourn an admissibility hearing to relieve against re-incarceration under CCRA s. 128(5)?
issues.applicant_position: Immigration Division may weigh the consequences of re-incarceration under Rule 43(2)(i) when deciding adjournments.
issues.respondent_position: Not stated directly; the Federal Court held the adjournment exceeded the Immigration Division's jurisdiction.
issues.result_quote: the issue raised by the appellant with regard to ss. 128(5) of the CCRA was clearly not a matter over which the Immigration Division had jurisdiction

issues.issue: Does the Charter (s. 7) argument change the result?
issues.applicant_position: Section 7 of the Charter requires the Immigration Division to consider whether re-incarceration would be unjust.
issues.respondent_position: Charter argument is improper to raise for the first time on this stay motion.
issues.result_quote: For the reasons which I have already stated, I need not address this issue in determining the merits of this motion.

issues.issue: Irreparable harm and balance of convenience for the stay.
issues.result_quote: As the appellant has not convinced me that his appeal raises a serious issue, I therefore need no address the two other prongs of the test
